prompt: Design a modern AI platform for building, testing, and deploying AI agents and assistants — browse a catalog of agent templates by capability and category, filter by rating and price, and open a template to see its description, features, model options, pricing, and developer reviews before launching your own agent. Make it feel cutting-edge, trustworthy, and clean.
title: Agent Atlas

issues.description: The planned and generated detail composition is gallery-led, but this product's detail object is an AI agent template rather than a media-rich listing. Universal detail law requires an info pane as the dominant moment for a record/task workflow; the gallery structure is Airbnb-shaped and does not serve the brief.

AmenityGrid renders every capability as a bordered card. On the detail screen this creates a second card cluster alongside the summary card, violating the one-card detail rule and making the page read like a generic template.

The supplied SCENES are abstract generated SVG geometry labeled as ecommerce scenes. They do not provide the human, photo-first visual language required by Airbnb and do not communicate an AI agent's workflow or capability.

The detail page inherits a photo gallery and commerce/listing structure even though the focused workflow is evaluating and launching an agent template. Replace listing-style media treatment with a branded workflow or configuration moment.
Status badges use hardcoded text-white instead of a theme foreground token, violating the universal no-hardcoded-colors rule and potentially weakening contrast against warning or success backgrounds.

Measured output reports missing Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono fonts. The selected design language specifies Plus Jakarta Sans for display and body, so the rendered typography is not brand-faithful.

The detail screen must show only Relay Support Triage. Any catalog metrics, other agent items, or cross-agent activity rendered in this screen would violate the hard one-item data contract; the detail composition should be explicitly scoped to the selected template.

The home catalog must visibly expose maintainer identity, review count, supported models, category/capability, availability, updated date, and price. A generic image card treatment alone is insufficient for the critical discovery and comparison workflow.

The focused workflow needs a clear launch handoff containing the selected model, Agent Atlas managed runtime deployment target, and required integrations before confirmation. These details must be visible near the Launch agent action rather than buried in unrelated sections.
The screen mixes an agent headline with a travel-booking form containing check-in, check-out, and guests. This is a recognizable Airbnb marketplace template and does not support agent discovery.
The six-card agent catalog is followed by another section titled 'Production-ready agents, in one catalog' and then another partial product card. This reads as duplicated catalog content.

The required compact discovery toolbar is not rendered correctly: there is no clear sort control, and filtering is split into an oversized travel-style form rather than the specified one-filter toolbar.
Several mounted catalog items have incomplete or misleading data, while the lower cards contain placeholder-like dollar symbols and 'Expires' labels that do not describe agent templates.

The visual system is a cold blue enterprise SaaS layout rather than the requested warm, friendly, trust-building language. The repeated abstract colored blocks also lack the photo-first/authored visual quality of the reference direction.

The hero and toolbar occupy a narrow left column with excessive unused space on the right, followed by a large gap before the catalog. The resulting proportions feel assembled rather than intentionally composed.
The detail screen is scoped to Relay Support Triage but its review rows describe multiple other agents, including LedgerExtract Pro, QuerySmith Analytics, PatchPilot, BriefForge, and SignalScout.
The detail pane uses booking concepts such as Dates, Guests, total price, and In stock. These are travel-commerce artifacts and are not legal or useful for an AI agent deployment detail.
The required model and cost comparison is absent. The screen does not show context limits, cost per 1,000 tasks, latency, or capability differences.
The focused detail workflow lacks a visible example workflow, concrete feature breakdown, tool requirements, deployment target summary, and launch handoff configuration.
The gallery is made of repetitive flat abstract blocks rather than meaningful agent workflow imagery or authored visuals. It does not establish a strong dominant moment for the template.
There is an unusually large blank region between the detail content and review list, weakening hierarchy and violating the intended alternating vertical rhythm.
The bottom 'Untitled' panel is an unexplained extra card outside the focused detail workflow and reads as an accidental duplicate or unfinished component.
HostTrustLegend is partially represented through trust bullets, but the required AmenityGrid is not visibly rendered as a complete, product-specific capabilities or requirements grid.
The measured layout reports that Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono are not loaded, while the design tokens require variable-driven font usage and the intended type system.

reviewResult.summary: The screens compile and the measured geometry is broadly sound, but the implementation over-applies Airbnb's gallery/listing patterns to an AI agent evaluation product. The detail screen violates the record-detail composition law, the amenity component creates excess card surfaces, imagery is abstract rather than meaningful, typography is not using the specified font, and token discipline is broken by hardcoded badge color. The result does not yet provide a trustworthy, focused path from agent evaluation to launch.
requiredFixes: In src/screens/detail.jsx, replace the gallery-led layout with an agent info pane as the dominant moment. Relay Support Triage is a task/template record, not a media-rich item; show purpose, workflow, trust signals, model options, requirements, and pricing instead of a photo gallery.

In src/screens/detail.jsx and src/components/AmenityGrid.jsx, convert the capability and requirement blocks from repeated bordered cards into divided fact rows or a restrained feature strip. The detail screen may have only one summary card.

In src/screens/home.jsx and src/screens/detail.jsx, replace the generated abstract ecommerce scene SVGs with product-specific agent visuals or remove the imagery where it does not add meaning. Do not present colored geometric blocks as photo-first media.
In src/components/ItemCard.jsx, remove the hardcoded text-white color and use the appropriate foreground token for status badges. Audit all status and accent text for WCAG AA contrast.

In src/screens/home.jsx and src/screens/detail.jsx, ensure the loaded font is Plus Jakarta Sans from the design language rather than the measured missing Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono fonts. Use the shared font tokens for all headings and body text.

In src/screens/detail.jsx, keep all visible pricing, reviews, model comparisons, integrations, maintainer details, and version history scoped exclusively to Relay Support Triage. Remove any catalog-wide metrics, other agent records, or marketplace discovery content from the detail view.

In src/screens/home.jsx, ensure the catalog visibly renders CatalogHighlights and ItemCard as required, with the five supplied agents showing capability, maintainer, rating, review count, supported models, status, updated date, and estimated task price.

In src/screens/detail.jsx, make Launch agent the single prominent action and keep Compare models as a quiet secondary action. Include deployment target, selected model, and required integrations in the launch handoff summary.
home: Replace the travel-style search form with the required agent discovery toolbar: keyword search, one category/rating/price filter control, and a relevance/rating/newest/cost sort control.
home: Remove the duplicated catalog section, the four unrelated summary metric cards, and the broken empty product card at the bottom; keep one coherent agent catalog workflow.
home: Add complete, specific agent card data including capability, maintainer, rating, review count, supported models, and starting price.
home: Replace the repeated abstract placeholder artwork with real, product-relevant agent visuals or authored media that does not resemble empty colored blocks.

detail: Rebuild the detail hero around one agent only, with a meaningful workflow visual, purpose, example workflow, features, model options, tool requirements, usage pricing, maintainer, reliability notes, and launch requirements.

detail: Remove the travel/commerce booking summary content such as Dates, Guests, In stock, and the $0.42 trip-style total; replace it with deployment target, selected model, integrations, estimated task cost, and a clear Launch agent action.
detail: Correct the reviews so every row refers to Relay Support Triage only; remove reviews naming LedgerExtract Pro, QuerySmith Analytics, PatchPilot, BriefForge, and SignalScout.
detail: Add the required supported-model comparison table with context limits, estimated cost per 1,000 tasks, latency notes, and capability differences.

detail: Make HostTrustLegend and AmenityGrid visibly meaningful for an AI marketplace by presenting verification/reliability signals and agent capabilities or requirements rather than travel-style amenity semantics.
detail: Eliminate the very large blank gap between the detail pane and reviews and restore the intended gallery → detail → CTA → feature/fact rows → reviews → trust-band rhythm.
detail and home: Load the specified theme fonts through CSS variables and correct the remaining off-grid alignments.
